issue.description:
Add the additive boolean auto_flush so a fleet detects the behaviour by handshake instead of inferring it from a version number.

The field reports the compiled default. A workspace that disables publication via checkpoint.auto_flush, and an invocation passing --no-auto-flush, do not change what the binary advertises; sync --status remains the only authority on whether a given workspace is clean.

Acceptance:
- auto_flush present once the default flips, absent before
- capability tests assert the advertised value matches actual binary behaviour
- documented as reporting the compiled default, not workspace state

Refs: plan section 11, 6.2.1; ADR-003.
issue.title: Advertise auto_flush in the capability document

issue.description:
Automatic flush introduces an outcome that does not exist today: the mutation succeeded and the checkpoint did not advance. Machine consumers must be able to tell that apart from the mutation not happening.

Acceptance:
- the mutation stays committed and visible
- the mutation's own success output is preserved on stdout
- the publication failure is reported on stderr
- the process exits 1, and exit 1 never implies rollback
- a test forces publication failure and asserts the mutation is still present

Refs: plan 6.2.1 item 5, section 5.2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Define split-failure semantics when a mutation commits and publication fails

issue.description:
Workspace discovery stops at the FIRST .beads directory on the upward walk and fails closed with a precise diagnostic when it lacks the bead-rs workspace fingerprint, instead of walking past a foreign store to an unrelated parent workspace. The diagnostic claims only that the directory is not a bead-rs workspace; identifying a foreign format stays prohibited. An explicit override permits legitimate nesting.

Motivated by the 2026-08-14 SEAM wrong-CLI-against-wrong-store incident class.

Acceptance:
- discovery terminates at any .beads directory encountered
- non-bead-rs .beads yields a fail-closed diagnostic naming the path, not the foreign format
- explicit override flag documented and tested for legitimate nesting
- section 4.1 discovery prose updated with the new rule

Refs: plan section 12 R030; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 3 dossier.
issue.title: R030: Self-defending workspace discovery (stop at first .beads, fail closed)

issue.description:
Issues may declare normalized local resource keys. A claim atomically acquires every key its bead declares and excludes ready issues needing a key currently held; release, close, and lease expiry return keys. Readiness explanations gain a resource-conflict reason code. Scope is strictly one native store: workspace-local scheduling exclusion, never distributed locking, and naming/documentation must say so.

Adopted from the run-1 deferral after NEEDLE ADR-015 made bead-level serialization the accepted shared-checkout model.

Acceptance:
- resource-key validation, acquisition/release lifecycle, and migration specified
- claim excludes conflicting ready work atomically inside the claim transaction
- explain/why report a resource-conflict reason code
- documentation anchors scope to a single workspace

Refs: plan section 12 R031; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 4 dossier; run-1 finalist 5.
issue.title: R031: Atomic resource locks

issue.description:
src/service/issues.rs:14 create_issue is the path main.rs cmd_create calls and it writes no row to events. Only the unused create_issue_internal (issues.rs:107) emits a created event.

Observed: after ~1620 bead create calls the events table held 0 rows and bead changes --latest reported max_sequence 0. This breaks the R013 change feed today, independently of any flush work, and would make an event-sequence dirtiness check silently no-op.

Acceptance:
- bead create appends exactly one created event in the same transaction as the insert
- bead changes --latest advances by one per create
- test asserts the event is rolled back with the issue when the transaction fails

Refs: plan 6.2 dirtiness contract, 6.2.1 P3; ADR-003.
issue.title: Emit an audit event from the public create_issue path

issue.description:
One verified read-only loader materializes a named checkpoint artifact (pointer, manifest, or monolith) into an ephemeral view serving: query against a historical generation without import; a semantic issue/event-level diff between two generations; and predicate-driven search across a generation series. Views are never accepted as import input; outputs are explicitly non-importable.

Acceptance:
- query --checkpoint PATH answers list/query against a committed generation read-only
- sync diff A B reports issue/event-level semantic delta between two generations
- archaeology outputs rejected by every import path
- loader reuses existing verification (hashes, counts, ordering) before serving any view

Refs: plan section 12 R029; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 8 dossier (archaeology).
issue.title: R029: Checkpoint archaeology (query/diff/bisect over committed generations)

issue.description:
Automatic flush makes concurrent workers contend on checkpoint publication, not just on SQLite. Publication needs its own serialization so a lost race degrades to success rather than to a torn pointer.

Acceptance:
- publication is serialized by a checkpoint lock separate from the SQLite write path
- a worker finding a newer generation already published for a sequence at or beyond its own treats it as success and exits 0
- bounded concurrent workers produce no torn pointer and no partially applied tombstone set
- at quiesce every worker's committed sequence is covered by some published generation

Refs: plan 6.2.1 item 4; ADR-003.
issue.title: Serialize checkpoint publication with a lock distinct from the SQLite write path

issue.description:
Close the class rather than the instances. A test walks the section 5 command contract, invokes each mutating command once against a fixture workspace, and asserts the live event sequence advances by at least one.

The test must fail when a newly added mutating command ships without an event, so this defect class cannot recur. Label-mutation paths are included.

Acceptance:
- every mutating command in the plan section 5 table is covered
- adding a mutating command without an event fails the suite
- read-only commands are asserted not to advance the sequence

Refs: plan 6.2.1 P3, section 5; ADR-003.
issue.title: Enumerate mutating commands and assert each advances the event sequence

issue.description:
Automatic flush must be a no-op when the covered sequence already equals the live event sequence, so a no-op mutation publishes no generation and creates no object.

This rule is only sound once every semantic mutation advances the sequence, which is why it depends on the event work.

Acceptance:
- a mutation that changes nothing publishes no new generation
- a real mutation publishes exactly one generation covering its own sequence
- sync flush-only against a clean checkpoint publishes nothing and exits 0

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 3 and 8; ADR-003.
issue.title: Skip automatic publication when the checkpoint already covers the live sequence

issue.description:
Every mutating command in main.rs independently discovers the workspace, opens its own rusqlite connection, commits, and prints. There is no shared path a publication step could hook.

Introduce one shared post-commit chokepoint so every present and future mutating command inherits identical publication behavior, rather than editing ~20 call sites. Publication runs after the transaction commits, never inside it, so a publication failure cannot roll back committed work. Read-only commands never publish.

Acceptance:
- one chokepoint, exercised by all mutating commands
- publication is strictly after commit
- read-only commands do not publish
- adding a mutating command inherits publication without touching its call site

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 1-2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Add a single post-commit checkpoint publication chokepoint

issue.description:
src/service/external_refs.rs contains no INSERT INTO events. ref add and ref remove commit semantic mutations without advancing the live event sequence.

Acceptance:
- ref add and ref remove each append one event in their own transaction
- event detail records namespace and key, and never the value verbatim if it can carry a credential-shaped string
- bead changes --latest advances per mutation

Refs: plan 6.2.1 P3; ADR-003.
issue.title: Emit audit events for external-reference mutations

issue.description:
create --unique-ref NAMESPACE:KEY binds an R011 external reference inside the insert transaction; when the reference is already bound, the command returns the existing bead's identity instead of creating a duplicate. The closed-bead case must be explicit (distinct output or flagged conflict) so automation cannot loop on finished work.

Prevents duplicate beads at the source when dispatchers materialize work from the same external identifier concurrently.

Acceptance:
- ref binding and duplicate detection occur in one insert transaction
- ref-hit returns the existing ID with output distinguishable from a fresh create
- closed-bead ref-hit semantics explicit and tested
- concurrent duplicate-create race test: exactly one bead exists afterwards

Refs: plan section 12 R032; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 5 dossier.
issue.title: R032: Idempotent create by unique reference (create --unique-ref)

issue.description:
src/service/dependencies.rs contains no INSERT INTO events. dep add and dep remove commit semantic mutations without advancing the live event sequence.

Acceptance:
- dep add and dep remove each append one event in their own transaction
- event detail records blocked, blocker, and kind
- bead changes --latest advances per mutation
- idempotent no-op dep add appends no event

Refs: plan 6.2.1 P3; ADR-003.
issue.title: Emit audit events for dependency mutations

issue.description:
src/service/data.rs contains no INSERT INTO events. data set and data remove commit semantic mutations without advancing the live event sequence.

Acceptance:
- data set and data remove each append one event in their own transaction
- event detail records namespace and schema_ref, not the document body
- bead changes --latest advances per mutation

Refs: plan 6.2.1 P3, R018; ADR-003.
issue.title: Emit audit events for structured-data mutations

issue.description:
src/service/checkpoint.rs:3567-3568 names the monolithic root objects/{generation_id}.jsonl, derived from the generation ID. Plan section 6.1.1 requires object filenames to contain their content SHA-256 so identical content is reused. The sharded writer already does this (checkpoint.rs:3741-3872); only the monolithic path diverges.

Observed: two consecutive flushes producing byte-identical content created two distinct objects (18 -> 20). Content-addressed reuse can never hit, so every flush leaks a full-workspace-sized immutable object.

Acceptance:
- monolithic root is named from its content SHA-256
- two publications of identical content produce exactly one object, asserted by count in a test
- existing generation-named objects remain readable, or a migration step is specified

Refs: plan 6.1.1, 6.2.1 P1; ADR-003.
issue.title: Content-address the monolithic checkpoint root object

issue.description:
A doctor scope reporting non-leased in_progress beads whose most recent event is older than a configured interval, together with the exact release remedy. Advisory only: doctor never releases work itself. This is the immediately executable subset of R019 starvation diagnostics for the non-leased majority of claims and must share reason codes with R001/R019 rather than inventing parallel semantics.

Acceptance:
- doctor scope lists stale non-leased in_progress beads with age and suggested command
- threshold is versioned workspace configuration
- stable diagnostic code shared with the R001 reason-code namespace
- leased beads excluded (R002 owns lease expiry)

Refs: plan section 12 R034; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 9 dossier.
issue.title: R034: Stale in-progress detection (doctor scope)

issue.description:
Plan section 6.2 step 6 requires applying pointer-declared tombstones once current.json is durable. They are declared and never applied.

Observed: current.json declared 18 deleted_paths and all 18 were still present on disk, and current.json wrongly listed itself among them. Ten mutate-and-flush cycles at ~1600 issues grew the checkpoint from 3 objects / 1.47 MB to 13 objects / 7.83 MB.

Acceptance:
- after a successful publication every path in deleted_paths is absent from disk
- current.json is never declared in its own deleted_paths (it belongs in replaced_paths)
- the retained object set is bounded by the generations current.json and previous.json reference
- sync --status reports unresolved tombstones and is not ready to commit while any remain
- cleanup is crash-safe and repeatable

Refs: plan 6.2 step 6, 6.2.1 P2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Apply pointer-declared checkpoint tombstones after the pointer commits

issue.description:
main.rs cmd_sync_flush_only hardcodes CheckpointMode::Monolithic, so the sharded publication path in checkpoint.rs is unreachable and every flush re-serializes the whole workspace. Flush is therefore linear in workspace size: 0.01s at 100 issues, 0.03s at 400, 0.07s at 1600.

Plan section 6.1.1 already specifies the thresholds (50,000 issue records, 64 MiB total, 8 MiB per record line) and the prefix-split partition plan, and specifies sealed append-only event tail objects so a frequently updated bead does not rewrite its history-bearing shard. Implement mode selection from the recorded thresholds, retaining an existing valid partition plan and splitting only overflowing shards.

Acceptance:
- mode is selected from recorded configuration/thresholds, not a constant
- crossing a threshold publishes a mode transition whose changed-path set includes the new root, objects, pointer replacement, and tombstones for the superseded root
- publication after one mutation writes bytes proportional to the changed shard plus event tail, demonstrated at two workspace sizes an order of magnitude apart
- monolithic and sharded restores are semantically equivalent

Refs: plan 6.1.1, 6.2.1 P4; ADR-003.
issue.title: Select sharded checkpoint mode from recorded thresholds instead of hardcoding monolithic

issue.description:
README, root help, the workflow summary in plan section 5.3, generated man pages, and AGENTS.md all state that nothing flushes implicitly. All of them become wrong the day the default flips and must change together. No partial reversal is permitted.

The surrounding environment's agent instructions (home CLAUDE.md) also carry the never-implicit-flush rule and need a corresponding update outside this repo; note it in the release, do not silently leave it stale.

Acceptance:
- no surviving never-implicit-flush wording in this repo once the default flips
- sync flush-only documented as an explicit idempotent check plus the --no-auto-flush hatch
- man pages regenerated and byte-reproducible
- help examples still parse under the existing help-example test

Refs: plan 5.3, 6.2.1; ADR-003.
issue.title: Reverse the never-implicit-flush documentation in the commit that flips the default

issue.description:
Recognize checkpoint-ahead-of-live-db after a git pull as a distinct remote-advanced state and add bead sync reconcile, which merges the pointer-verified checkpoint into the live store via the existing --merge machinery. First deliverable is the normative state taxonomy: only a verified pointer whose event stream is a superset of live state qualifies; every other covered-ahead-of-live case remains a fail-closed integrity failure exactly as today.

Acceptance:
- state taxonomy specified and independently reviewable before implementation
- sync reconcile merges a verified-superset checkpoint into the live store
- all other covered>live cases still fail closed; doctor distinguishes remote-advanced from integrity failure
- bead-rs still never runs Git

Refs: plan section 12 R027; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 1.
issue.title: R027: Remote-advanced checkpoint reconcile (bead sync reconcile)

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: /home/coding/bead-rs/docs/plan/plan.md (section 6.2.1, R026, section 13 activation gate)
Authorized by: docs/adr/003-automatic-checkpoint-flush-gated-on-incremental-publication.md

## Overview
Make a successful semantic mutation publish a checkpoint generation covering its own committed sequence, replacing explicit sync flush-only as the default, so the durable checkpoint is never silently behind the database.

Gated. Per-mutation publication against the current path would write bytes quadratic in mutation count into a Git-tracked directory: flush is linear in workspace size, each generation leaks a full-workspace-sized object that is never collected, and most mutation kinds never advance the sequence that signals a flush is needed. The prerequisites are the implementation converging on plan sections 6.1.1 and 6.2 as already written; each is worth fixing whether or not the default ever changes.

bead-rs still never invokes Git. Automatic Git publication remains rejected.

## Progress
- [ ] P1: content-addressed monolithic root
- [ ] P2: applied pointer-declared tombstones
- [ ] P3: audit event for every committed semantic mutation (create, dep, ref, data, enumeration test)
- [ ] P4: reachable sharded publication
- [ ] A1-A6: chokepoint, skip-when-clean, publication lock, split-failure semantics, escape hatches, capability handshake
- [ ] A7: documentation reversal
- [ ] A8: activation gate evidence, then flip the default
issue.title: Genesis: R026 Automatic Checkpoint Flush Implementation

issue.description:
Escape hatches for the automatic default. --no-auto-flush suppresses publication for one invocation; checkpoint.auto_flush suppresses it durably for a workspace; the flag wins over configuration.

Acceptance:
- either mechanism leaves the checkpoint dirty exactly as explicit-flush behaviour does today
- sync --status reports the resulting dirty state
- the flag overrides the configuration key in both directions
- automatic publication stays silent on success, so bead create still prints only the ID plus LF

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 6-7, section 5 command table; ADR-003.
issue.title: Add --no-auto-flush and the checkpoint.auto_flush workspace configuration key

issue.description:
Validate a versioned JSON manifest composed strictly of existing command primitives (creates, updates, labels, dependencies, closes) with local references for newly created IDs; show a dry-run diff; then commit all operations in one transaction that publishes at most one checkpoint generation under R026. v1 must refuse any semantics a single existing command does not already have.

Adopted from the run-1 deferral: per-mutation publication makes N-command materialization N generations, and interrupted materializations still discard entire disposable workspaces.

Acceptance:
- manifest v1 schema specified as thin composition of existing primitives
- dry-run reports the full semantic delta without mutation
- commit is all-or-none in one transaction, one checkpoint generation
- result map links manifest entries to created/updated IDs

Refs: plan section 12 R033; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 6 dossier; run-1 finalist 6.
issue.title: R033: Atomic bulk transaction manifests

issue.description:
Add bead sync fork: an explicit operator command that re-origins a cloned workspace under a new store UUID recorded in a provenance-chained receipt, so clones of one repository become distinct origins whose event streams merge composably under existing different-UUID rules instead of being rejected as same-UUID divergence.

Acceptance:
- fork receipt fields and UUID derivation provenance specified
- forked clone merges into the origin workspace cleanly via existing merge rules
- doctor detects same-UUID divergence and names the fork/reconcile remedy
- forking is never implicit or inferred

Refs: plan section 12 R028; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 2.
issue.title: R028: Fork identity for cloned workspaces (bead sync fork)

issue.description:
Run the plan section 13 R026 activation gate and record its evidence. The default may not flip until every criterion passes at one commit.

Criteria: bounded objects across at least 1,000 mutate-and-publish cycles with checkpoint bytes within a recorded constant factor of the live workspace; applied tombstones with none unresolved; sound dirtiness across every mutating command; incremental cost at two workspace sizes an order of magnitude apart with the section 3.5.10 rapid-fire benchmarks inside budget; concurrency with no torn pointer and no lost mutation; split-failure semantics; both escape hatches; doctor --rehearse passing against a workspace built entirely through automatic publication; and the capability handshake plus documentation reversal.

Acceptance:
- every gate criterion has recorded evidence at one commit
- evidence is committed to the repository, not left as a local artifact
- a failing criterion leaves the explicit-flush default in place

Refs: plan section 13 R026 activation gate; ADR-003.
issue.title: Produce R026 activation gate evidence
